title: Sequence liability motifs for antibodies and protein biologics
notes: Every rule is a MOTIF MATCH with a citation. A match is a site to look at, never a verdict:
the rate of any of these reactions depends on local structure, formulation pH, excipients and
temperature, none of which a sequence contains.
The deamidation rules are ordered by their published relative rate (NG fastest, then NS, then
NT) and that order is the only ranking this pack asserts. `risk` is a rank index, not a rate.
Exposure weighting is applied ONLY when a structure is supplied: without one, exposureKnown is
false and the flag says exposure is unknown rather than assuming the site is on the surface.

rules.label: N-linked glycosylation sequon (N-X-S/T, X != P)
rules.citation: Gavel Y, von Heijne G. Sequence differences between glycosylated and non-glycosylated Asn-X-Thr/Ser acceptor sites. Protein Eng 3:433-442 (1990). Proline at X blocks transfer.

rules.label: Asn deamidation, fastest published sequence context (N-G)
rules.citation: Robinson NE, Robinson AB. Molecular clocks: deamidation of asparaginyl and glutaminyl residues in peptides and proteins. PNAS 98:944-949 (2001); Asn-Gly is the fastest of the 20 C-terminal-neighbour contexts.

rules.label: Asn deamidation, intermediate published context (N-S)
rules.citation: Robinson NE, Robinson AB. PNAS 98:944-949 (2001); Asn-Ser deamidates more slowly than Asn-Gly and faster than Asn-Thr.

rules.label: Asn deamidation, slower published context (N-T)
rules.citation: Robinson NE, Robinson AB. PNAS 98:944-949 (2001); the beta-branched Thr neighbour slows succinimide formation.

rules.label: Asp isomerization / succinimide (D-G)
rules.citation: Wakankar AA, Borchardt RT. Formulation considerations for proteins susceptible to asparagine deamidation and aspartate isomerization. J Pharm Sci 95:2321-2336 (2006).

rules.label: Asp isomerization / succinimide (D-S)
rules.citation: Wakankar AA, Borchardt RT. J Pharm Sci 95:2321-2336 (2006).

rules.label: Asp isomerization / succinimide (D-T)
rules.citation: Wakankar AA, Borchardt RT. J Pharm Sci 95:2321-2336 (2006).

rules.label: Acid-labile Asp-Pro peptide bond (fragmentation)
rules.citation: Vlasak J, Ionescu R. Fragmentation of monoclonal antibodies. mAbs 3:253-263 (2011); the Asp-Pro bond is the classic acid-labile site.

rules.label: Methionine oxidation (solvent-exposed Met)
rules.citation: Chumsae C et al. Comparison of methionine oxidation in thermal stability and chemically stressed samples of a fully human monoclonal antibody. J Chromatogr B 850:285-294 (2007).

rules.label: Tryptophan oxidation (solvent-exposed Trp)
rules.citation: Hensel M et al. Identification of potential sites for tryptophan oxidation in recombinant antibodies. PLoS ONE 6:e17708 (2011).

rules.label: Unpaired cysteine (odd cysteine count in the domain)
rules.citation: Zhang W, Czupryn MJ. Free sulfhydryl in recombinant monoclonal antibodies. Biotechnol Prog 18:509-513 (2002).

rules.label: N-terminal Glu/Gln, pyroglutamate formation (-17.0265 Da from Gln, -18.0106 from Glu)
rules.citation: Liu YD et al. N-terminal glutamate to pyroglutamate conversion in vivo for human IgG2 antibodies. J Biol Chem 286:11211-11217 (2011).

rules.label: C-terminal lysine clipping (heavy-chain charge heterogeneity)
rules.citation: Dick LW et al. C-terminal lysine variants in fully human monoclonal antibodies. Biotechnol Bioeng 100:1132-1143 (2008).

rules.label: Lysine glycation motif (Lys next to an acidic residue)
rules.citation: Quan C et al. A study in glycation of a therapeutic recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody. Anal Biochem 373:179-191 (2008).

rules.label: RGD integrin-binding motif
rules.citation: Ruoslahti E. RGD and other recognition sequences for integrins. Annu Rev Cell Dev Biol 12:697-715 (1996).

exposureNote: Relative side-chain accessibility above this fraction of the Tien et al. 2013 theoretical maximum counts as exposed. It is a display threshold, not a rate.
